findings.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:7 — The move converts an intra-file call (mark_failed_threshold -> create_issue_platform_occurrence in the same module) into a new top-level, import-time dependency of incidents.py on incident_occurrence.py, adding a fresh module edge that didn't exist before and that could turn into a real circular-import hazard if incident_occurrence.py (or its transitive deps) is later changed to need anything from incidents.py/mark_failed.py; not verifiable as an existing cycle in this trimmed checkout since sentry.monitors.models and sentry.signals aren't present here.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/mark_failed.py:11 — logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` is copy-pasted into mark_failed.py, incidents.py, and incident_occurrence.py but none of the three files ever call `logger.*`, so the refactor triples a pre-existing orphaned logger instead of dropping it.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:28 — Renaming `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence` drops the explicit "issue platform" wording and now reads as if it operates on/creates a `MonitorIncident`, which is misleading since the function actually builds and produces an `IssueOccurrence` keyed off an existing incident.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:1 — The new module `sentry.monitors.logic.incident_occurrence` has a name nearly identical to the unrelated existing module `sentry.issues.issue_occurrence` it imports from internally, creating a naming-collision/confusion risk for future imports and search.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:109 — produce_occurrence_to_kafka is called with no try/except, no timeout, and no retry, so any Kafka producer error propagates uncaught out of create_incident_occurrence and up through try_incident_threshold into the cron task (behavior carried over unchanged from the pre-refactor create_issue_platform_occurrence, so not a new regression but still a live gap in the reorganized module).

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:11 — logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) is declared but never used anywhere in incidents.py, so failures/edge cases in try_incident_threshold (e.g. muted skip, non-ERROR/OK/ACTIVE status skip, get_or_create races) produce no diagnostic log trail.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:25 — logger = logging.getLogger(__name__) is declared but never used anywhere in incident_occurrence.py, so a Kafka produce failure in create_incident_occurrence would only surface as an unhandled exception rather than a logged, attributable error.

src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:57 — monitor_env.save(update_fields=("status",)) and the MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create call on lines 62-70 have no exception handling; a transient DB error here raises uncaught out of try_incident_threshold and thus out of mark_failed, breaking the calling cron check-in task (pre-existing behavior preserved by the move, not newly introduced).

goldens.comment: The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.
The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:7 — The move converts an intra-file call (mark_failed_threshold -> create_issue_platform_occurrence in the same module) into a new top-level, import-time dependency of incidents.py on incident_occurrence.py, adding a fresh module edge that didn't exist before and that could turn into a real circular-import hazard if incident_occurrence.py (or its transitive deps) is later changed to need anything from incidents.py/mark_failed.py; not verifiable as an existing cycle in this trimmed checkout since sentry.monitors.models and sentry.signals aren't present here.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new module-level dependency: `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py` now imports `create_incident_occurrence` from the new `incident_occurrence.py` (`from sentry.monitors.logic.incident_occurrence import create_incident_occurrence`). Previously, the occurrence-creation logic lived in the same file as the incident-threshold logic (old `mark_failed.py`), so this particular import edge did not exist. While the finding’s claim of a *current* circular import is not verifiable from the diff alone, the new top-level import does create a tighter coupling and a plausible future circular-import hazard if `incident_occurrence.py` (or its transitive imports) later needs `incidents.py` or `mark_failed.py`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` in `mark_failed.py`, `incidents.py`, and `incident_occurrence.py` without any `logger.*` usage in those files. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incident_occurrence.py:28 — Renaming `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence` drops the explicit "issue platform" wording and now reads as if it operates on/creates a `MonitorIncident`, which is misleading since the function actually builds and produces an `IssueOccurrence` keyed off an existing incident.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the function was moved and renamed to `create_incident_occurrence`, and it indeed accepts a `MonitorIncident` and uses it (e.g., `fingerprint=[incident.grouphash]`, tag `monitor.incident`, etc.) while producing an `IssueOccurrence`. Calling it an “incident occurrence” is not verifiably misleading from the diff alone—it’s a naming/style preference rather than a concrete, diff-provable problem in behavior or design.

While there is no direct runtime collision shown in the diff, the near-identical names (`incident_occurrence` vs `issue_occurrence`) are likely to cause future developer confusion in imports/search/grep, making it a concrete maintainability concern grounded in the new file/module naming.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:57 — monitor_env.save(update_fields=("status",)) and the MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create call on lines 62-70 have no exception handling; a transient DB error here raises uncaught out of try_incident_threshold and thus out of mark_failed, breaking the calling cron check-in task (pre-existing behavior preserved by the move, not newly introduced).

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` the diff shows `monitor_env.save(update_fields=("status",))` and `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(...)` are executed without any local exception handling. While this is not necessarily a defect (many codepaths intentionally let DB exceptions propagate), it is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness concern that transient DB failures would bubble up out of `mark_failed` via this new helper. The claim about breaking a specific cron task is not verifiable from the diff, and the behavior appears preserved from the moved code.
